knowledge_graph.title: COVID-19 vaccination in Ghana
knowledge_graph.description: COVID-19 vaccination in Ghana began on 1 March 2021 after the country became the first recipient of the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine as part of the COVAX initiative. As of 6 June 2021, Ghana had administered 1,230,000 vaccine doses.

related_questions.question: Do I need a vaccine to travel to Ghana?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, some vaccinations are recommended or required for travel to Ghana. Specifically, yellow fever vaccination is required for all travelers over nine months of age. Additionally, certain other vaccines are recommended depending on individual risk factors and the nature of the trip.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, some vaccinations are recommended or required for travel to Ghana

list.snippet: Yellow Fever: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required for entry into Ghana, and it must be issued at least 10 days before your arrival.

list.title: Hepatitis A and Typhoid:
list.snippet: These are recommended for most travelers to Ghana due to the potential for food and waterborne illnesses.

list.title: Routine Vaccinations:
list.snippet: It's important to ensure routine vaccinations like measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR), tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis (Tdap), and polio are up to date.

list.title: Hepatitis B:
list.snippet: Considered for long-term travelers or those at risk of exposure.

list.title: Meningitis:
list.snippet: Recommended for travel during the dry season (December to June) due to the meningitis belt in the region.

list.title: Malaria:
list.snippet: While there isn't a vaccine for malaria, preventative medication and mosquito bite precautions are strongly advised.

list.title: COVID-19:
list.snippet: Check the latest requirements for COVID-19 vaccination and testing as they may vary.

list.title: Rabies:
list.snippet: Vaccination is recommended for travelers at high risk of animal bites or contact.

list.title: Food and water safety:
list.snippet: Practice good hygiene, such as washing hands frequently and being cautious about food and water sources, is essential to avoid illnesses.

text_blocks.snippet: It's strongly recommended to consult with a doctor or travel clinic at least 4-8 weeks before your trip to discuss specific vaccination needs and other health precautions.
